panels.title: Redis replay results per second
panels.description: One observation per Redis replay lookup. Subscribe and continuity repair are separate. Gap includes retention, epoch mismatch, replay cap and a missing required-through position. Failed includes dependency and invalid payload errors which the current store interface does not distinguish.

panels.title: Replay and room catchup p95
panels.description: Redis lookup with cursor and required-through continuity validation. Join catchup also includes buffered-live handoff. Continuity repair runs after feed restoration, live gaps and quiet position checks. Percentiles overlap and cannot be added.

panels.title: Replay events and broker feed results
panels.description: Subscribe counts each event accepted by a recipient queue. Continuity counts each valid replay item offered to room fanout once per room, independent of recipient count or queue acceptance. The populations have different units.

panels.title: Redis replay payload byte rate
panels.description: Encoded event payload bytes. Subscribe counts successful recipient queue admissions; continuity counts valid items offered to room fanout once per room. Neither includes WebSocket framing or control traffic.

panels.description: Use the selected time range to correlate this signal with workload, scrape health and related stages. Idle event counters may have no series until their first event.

panels.title: WebSocket setup p95
panels.description: Gateway handler entry through accepted setup or failure. Accepted timing ends before the read loop and excludes the socket lifetime. Includes only setup requests reaching Go.

panels.title: WebSocket setup stage p95
panels.description: Only entered setup stages are observed. Ready means the stage finished; final setup outcomes remain separate. Admission includes ticket verification, origin, local capacity and Redis handshake rate limiting. Setup stage percentiles cannot be added.

description: Operational triage for the local Messenger deployment. Scrape coverage, workload and timing boundaries are distinct signals.
